# Feasibility, architecture and correlated allocations {#sec-feasibility-allocations}

A receiver can have enough gain, a precise phase estimate and a fast data link,
yet still fail its task. The gain may clip the blocker, the phase may select the
wrong spatial branch, or the estimate may arrive after the scene has changed.
Architecture selection starts by intersecting these conditions at the same
operating point. A favorable calculation in each of several incompatible states
is not a feasible receiver.

This bounded development asks whether a small direction-comparison receiver can
meet a supplied angular, blocker and response-time brief. The reader should be
able to turn a need into a conditioned observable, calculate incompatible gain
and information constraints, compare interface/resource alternatives, and state
which missing evidence prevents a hardware recommendation. Requirement framing
begins in [Chapter 1](phase-comparison.qmd#sec-requirement-framing). We use
[Chapter 5](phase-delay-inference.qmd) to separate precision from ambiguity,
[Chapter 6](model-adequacy-uncertainty.qmd) to qualify approximations, and
[Chapters 8–10](fields-geometry-transduction.qmd) for field, disturbance and
extraction interfaces. Numerical envelopes below are **synthetic design inputs**,
not selected products or measured receiver performance.

## Joint feasible regions {#sec-joint-feasibility}

### A brief that can fail

Suppose one far-field, linearly polarized narrowband source near 1 GHz is to be
located within a known front sector $|\theta|\leq60^\circ$. The observable is
source direction relative to the array normal at the record midpoint, inferred
from simultaneous, orientation-normalized channel voltages. A single plane-wave
manifold is supplied; multipath, unknown polarization and installation errors
must eventually be tested rather than included by assertion. Use rounded
propagation speed $3.00\times10^8$ m/s, hence wavelength $\lambda=0.300$ m.
The following is an illustrative operational brief, not a project requirement.

| Condition or limit | Supplied value and meaning |
|---|---|
| Wanted input and blocker at RF ports P0 | Wanted tone near 1.000 GHz, −100 dBm/channel; one CW blocker near 1.010 GHz, −20 dBm/channel; each tuning-offset uncertainty at most 100 Hz |
| Angular task | Local standard uncertainty at most 0.5° near the sector edge, conditional on the correct branch; branch-error probability at most $10^{-3}$; blocker-induced angular bias at most 0.02° |
| Time and dynamics | Report within 5 ms of record start; post-record processing/transfer 0.6 ms; angular excursion during a constant-manifold record at most 0.05°, with supplied rate bound 20°/s |
| Residual carrier offset | At most 100 Hz after supplied coarse tuning; no claim that a shared clock removes it |
| Noise/energy interface | Per-channel coherent tone SNR $\rho=100$ in 1 ms at zero offset after the selected front end; independent proper Gaussian channel noise, fixed phase and no fades |
| Digitizer interface P2 | Weak-tone floor −60 dBm; maximum composite peak voltage 0.100 V into an effective 50 Ω, equivalent to −10 dBm CW power; both are supplied qualified-interface limits |
| Complete observation interface | Desired positive-frequency component retained and orientation normalized; sum of magnitudes of all blocker-to-record image/alias paths, including conversion/filtering and the finite record, at most $10^{-5}$ of the wanted response |
| Resources | Total receiver 2.5 W; sustained link 5 Gbit/s including framing; three simultaneous channels allowed |

The specified noise SNR is after the complete observation in the selected 46 dB
gain state; another gain/filter state needs its own input-referred noise and
observation-noise gain. The noise interface can equivalently specify a wanted power −102 dBm at the
preselector output P1 and an effective power density −152 dBm/Hz there. Their
ratio is $C/N_0=10^5$ Hz and the ideal coherent tone observation gives
$\rho=(C/N_0)T$. That density must include the actual filter, amplifier and
converter-referred contributions; a passive insertion loss is not noiseless.
The stated density is an input requiring evidence, not a derivation from the
blocker level or a nominal noise figure. Chapter 9 constructs such contributions.

The weak-tone floor at P2 is likewise a supplied interface contract. Fourteen
stored bits below will set link traffic, **not** establish this floor or effective
resolution. Kester's [MT-001](https://www.analog.com/media/en/training-seminars/tutorials/MT-001.pdf),
Rev. A, p. 1, identifies the ideal converter and decorrelation assumptions behind
its quantization-noise model. It supplies no guarantee for the proposed blocker
and weak-tone combination. Driver loading, overload recovery, actual noise and
spurs remain implementation evidence needs.

For architecture variables $\mathbf x$ and environmental/state inputs
$\boldsymbol\eta$, write the conditional feasible set as

$$
 \mathcal F(\boldsymbol\eta)=
 \{\mathbf x:g_r(\mathbf x,\boldsymbol\eta)\leq0\ \text{for every required }r\}.
$$

An empty set rejects that combination of requirements, assumptions and available
alternatives. A nonempty model set is **conditional** until its technology,
physical inputs and task mapping are supported. If $\boldsymbol\eta$ lies in a
justified bounded set $\mathcal E$, robustness means satisfying the constraints
for every $\boldsymbol\eta\in\mathcal E$; choosing the most favorable unknown
value proves only existence of an optimistic case. An unspecified nuisance
cannot be silently assigned zero.

For a fixed architecture this distinction is $\exists\mathbf x\,
\forall\boldsymbol\eta\in\mathcal E$, not
$\forall\boldsymbol\eta\,\exists\mathbf x$. An adaptive architecture must
include its allowed sensing, state changes, latency and policies among the design
variables before claiming that it handles different conditions.

### Gain does not create headroom

First intersect weak-tone visibility and composite-input survival. Let $G$ be
the conversion/voltage-chain **power gain in dB** between equal 50 Ω reference
planes, $L_s$ the wanted insertion loss, and $A_B$ the blocker's total RF
attenuation in dB. At the gain input, powers in milliwatts are

$$
 p_s=10^{(-100-L_s)/10},\qquad p_b=10^{(-20-A_B)/10}.
$$

With worst relative tone phase, the peak voltage is proportional to
$\sqrt{p_s}+\sqrt{p_b}$. Thus the equivalent composite peak power before gain is
$p_{\rm pk}=(\sqrt{p_s}+\sqrt{p_b})^2$, and the two bounds are

$$
 G_{\min}=-60-(-100-L_s)=40+L_s,\qquad
 G_{\max}=-10-10\log_{10}p_{\rm pk}.
$$

This is a peak constraint, not an incoherent addition of average powers. For
more carriers replace the two amplitudes by a justified envelope or crest-factor
bound. Gain must exist in $[G_{\min},G_{\max}]$ and every intermediate stage must
also survive the waveform. Final-output headroom alone cannot establish that.

With no preselection, $L_s=A_B=0$: the bounds are 40 and 9.99913 dB. Their
intersection is empty by approximately 30 dB. A digital blocker notch after
sampling cannot restore clipped information. Now supply a selector family with
$L_s=2$ dB, and choose $A_B=40$ dB. The bounds become 42 and 49.93128 dB.
At $G=46$ dB, wanted and blocker powers at P2 are −56 and −14 dBm; the
worst composite is −13.93128 dBm, within the supplied −10 dBm limit.
The gain interval is now nonempty, conditional on linearity and noise evidence.

@fig-gain-feasibility shows how attenuation creates an interval rather than
merely changing a nominal operating point. Reducing $A_B$ to 30 dB while retaining
2 dB wanted loss leaves $G_{\max}\simeq39.98$ dB, still below 42 dB.
The architecture needs attenuation at the correct plane, not a larger gain
number or a cleaner output after clipping. The simplified first-stage input
survival envelope is −15 dBm; the selected branch sees a −60 dBm blocker, but
an actual stage-by-stage gain/drive allocation is still required.

The weak-tone lower bound stays at42dB for a selector with2dB wanted loss. The composite-peak upper bound rises with attenuation and crosses the lower bound near32dB. ### Information, ambiguity and available time

A baseline $d$ along the array axis has relative field phase
$\phi=kd\sin\theta$, where $k=2\pi/\lambda$, using Chapter 8's sourceward
geometry and Chapter 1's normalized orientation. A phase report is modulo $2\pi$.
To avoid two noiseless directions in the closed sector sharing the same phase,
require

$$
 2kd\sin60^\circ<2\pi,\qquad
 d<d_{\rm amb}={\lambda\over2\sin60^\circ}=0.173205\ \mathrm m.
$$

The inequality is strict: equality aliases the two sector endpoints. This is a
single-baseline, single-frequency result under the supplied manifold, not a
universal aperture limit.

For a sufficiently strong tone with proper Gaussian complex noise, Chapter 2's
small-noise phase approximation gives per-channel phase variance $1/(2\rho)$.
Independent equal-noise channels therefore have relative-phase variance
$1/\rho$. Linearizing the phase-angle relation gives

$$
 \sigma_\theta\simeq{1\over kd|\cos\theta|\sqrt\rho},\qquad
 d\geq d_{\rm prec}={1\over k|\cos\theta|\sigma_{\theta,\max}\sqrt\rho}.
$$

Use radians in this calculation. At the edge approached from inside the sector,
$|\cos\theta|=1/2$, $\sigma_{\theta,\max}=0.00872665$ rad and $\rho=100$:
$d_{\rm prec}=1.094269$ m. There is no baseline satisfying both 1.094269 m
minimum precision aperture and 0.173205 m maximum unambiguous baseline. A local
precision calculation alone would have selected a globally ambiguous design.
The linearized uncertainty is conditional on the correct branch; it is not a
Gaussian model for arbitrarily large angle errors or an edge-clipped estimator.

Increasing gain does not improve this input-referred SNR when signal and dominant
analog noise are amplified together. Increasing observation time can improve
energy, but the time must exist. For a normalized rectangular tone observation
with residual frequency $\delta f$, direct integration of
$T^{-1}\int_0^T e^{j2\pi\delta f t}dt$ gives amplitude
$e^{j\pi\delta fT}\operatorname{sinc}(\delta fT)$, with
$\operatorname{sinc}x=\sin(\pi x)/(\pi x)$. Consequently

$$
 \rho(T,\delta f)=(10^5\,\mathrm{Hz})T\operatorname{sinc}^2(\delta fT).
$$

This is an explicit observation model, not a universal integration-loss rule.
The constant-manifold excursion requirement gives $T\leq0.05/20=2.5$ ms;
latency alone gives $T\leq4.4$ ms. Thus 2.5 ms is the tighter supplied limit.
A short baseline $d_s=0.150$ m would need $\rho=5321.885$ even before other
errors: 53.21885 ms at zero offset. It cannot obtain that energy within the
brief. At 100 Hz residual offset and 1 ms, $\rho=96.75312$ rather than 100.
Both the wanted response and noise normalization must follow the observation.

@fig-aperture-feasibility makes the precision/ambiguity conflict visible.
A 1.2 m baseline meets the local 0.5° target at 1 ms, but its wrapped phase
cannot select the correct direction. A 0.15 m baseline resolves the sector but
cannot meet that precision with the available energy. More information, a
restricted sector, a changed deadline/energy envelope or another measured
observable is needed.

## Architecture and quantitative interfaces {#sec-architecture-interfaces}

Consider three simultaneous ports at positions 0, 0.15 and 1.20 m. The long
baseline supplies local precision, while the short baseline supplies a coarse
sector estimate. This is a bounded ambiguity-restoration example, not a complete
bearing estimator or a claim that three elements solve multipath/polarization.
The source amplitude/common phase is a nuisance removed by relative comparisons.
A single analog-combined complex output cannot generally recover direction from
one unknown complex source amplitude: for any nonzero combined response $b(u)$,
its change can be absorbed into that amplitude. Multiple independent beam outputs
or scans can restore information, but their timing and manifold must be budgeted.
Analog reception is a valid alternative when those interfaces are supplied.

For the selected simultaneous case let $u=\sin\theta$ and
$\Delta u=\lambda/d_l=0.25$ be long-baseline branch spacing. Fine candidates
come from adding integer cycles to its phase; select the one nearest the short
baseline's direction cosine. Ignoring channel-noise correlation would misstate
that decision's uncertainty: both differences contain the reference channel.
If individual small phase errors $\epsilon_0,\epsilon_s,\epsilon_l$ are
independent with variance $1/(2\rho)$, the branch-comparison error is

$$
 e_u={\epsilon_s-\epsilon_0\over kd_s}
       -{\epsilon_l-\epsilon_0\over kd_l},\qquad
 \sigma_{e_u}^2={1\over\rho}
 \left[{1\over(kd_s)^2}+{1\over(kd_l)^2}-{1\over(kd_s)(kd_l)}\right].
$$

The cross term follows from the shared $\epsilon_0$ source; it is not an arbitrary
correlation coefficient. In the high-SNR Gaussian phase approximation,
$2\Phi[-\Delta u/(2\sigma_{e_u})]$ bounds a nearest-branch error when the coarse
phase has not wrapped, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF. To avoid treating
that qualification as automatic, add a coarse-wrap bound. The minimum distance
to its principal-phase boundary over the sector is
$m=\pi-kd_s\sin60^\circ$. A conservative union bound is

$$
 P_{\rm branch}\ \lesssim\
 2\Phi\!\left(-{\Delta u\over2\sigma_{e_u}}\right)
 +2\Phi(-m\sqrt\rho).
$$

The approximate sign recalls the linear Gaussian phase model, not a measured
error rate. At 1 ms and worst 100 Hz residual offset, the two terms are
$4.258\times10^{-5}$ and $3.472\times10^{-5}$, totaling less than
$7.74\times10^{-5}$, below the supplied $10^{-3}$ limit. The long-baseline
local uncertainty is approximately 0.46353°. No calibration, multipath or state
error has yet been charged; the apparent margin is not available twice.
A branch failure is a large error event, not another small term to RSS into 0.46353°.

### The blocker must also pass through the observation

The preceding numbers omit retained blocker contamination. Headroom alone does
not justify that omission. After the RF selector the blocker is 42 dB above the
wanted tone, an amplitude ratio $R_B=10^{42/20}=125.8925$. For example, if a
changed operating condition placed it 100.5 kHz from the wanted tone and no
additional rejection were supplied, a 1 ms rectangular observation would retain
$R_B|\operatorname{sinc}(100.5)|=0.39873$ times the wanted amplitude. That can
change the phase and even the selected spatial branch without clipping.
Receiver passband width is not a statement of stopband rejection.

The brief therefore specifies the **composite** observation amplitude ratio
$\eta_B\leq10^{-5}$ at the allowed 1.010 GHz blocker frequencies, relative to
the wanted response. This −100 dB amplitude-transfer specification bounds the sum of path magnitudes for both
real-signal images and any aliased route into the reported record; it is not
merely a digital-filter attenuation at one nominal frequency. The 200 kHz IF
width below is a receiver passband, not an assumed arbitrary modulated waveform.
The calculation here remains a tone comparison. A real implementation must
demonstrate this rejection across frequency/state while preserving the assumed
wanted gain and the full observation noise SNR. Its filtering/digital extraction
is included in the supplied 0.6 ms processing and power envelopes; whether a
specific implementation meets all of them remains unknown.

With that contract, normalize each wanted record mean to a unit phasor. The
retained blocker phasor has magnitude at most
$r=R_B\eta_B=0.00125893$. A circle of radius $r<1$ about the wanted phasor has
maximum phase departure $\beta=\sin^{-1}r$ (the ray tangent to that circle).
Its minimum amplitude is $1-r$. Thus the long-baseline phase bias is bounded
by $2\beta$, corresponding to approximately 0.01149° angle bias near 60°,
below the separate 0.02° blocker allocation. Use the actual inverse sine of
the perturbed direction cosine if a local angle approximation is inadequate.

For a conservative high-SNR noise calculation use
$\rho_{\min}=\rho(1-r)^2=96.50966$, giving local uncertainty about 0.46412°.
Let $\sigma_{e_u,{\rm wc}}$ denote the earlier error SD calculated using this
reduced SNR, and bound the branch-comparison mean displacement by
$b_u=2\beta[1/(kd_s)+1/(kd_l)]$. Subtract these bias allowances from the
decision margins before computing tails:

$$
 P_{\rm branch}\ \lesssim\
 2\Phi\!\left(-{\Delta u/2-b_u\over\sigma_{e_u,{\rm wc}}}\right)
 +2\Phi[-(m-2\beta)\sqrt{\rho_{\min}}]
 <8.90\times10^{-5}.
$$

This requires positive margins and retains the Gaussian phase approximation;
it is a conditional model bound, not an empirical error rate. The conservative
baseline bias bounds do not assume independent blocker phases. @fig-blocker-observation shows why RF survival and retained interference are
separate constraints. Other reference, calibration, environmental and manifold
errors remain to be allocated. If the
composite rejection is unavailable, the candidate's information closure remains
open even though its headroom interval is nonempty.

A phasor disk gives the worst phase bias and the minimum retained mean amplitude.](figures/blocker-observation.svg){#fig-blocker-observation fig-alt="Retained blocker-to-wanted amplitude falls with composite observation rejection. The chosen analog-converted interface supplies a real 20 MHz IF with 200 kHz
receiver passband, sampled ideally at 100 MS/s, with 14 stored bits/sample.
Correct conversion orientation and reset phase are required interface conditions;
the end-to-end transfer treatment constructs them before allocations close.
Every channel includes the selector before gain/conversion. Equal nominal
frequencies are insufficient without the same spectral orientation, phase epoch
and known sample identity. The following resource values are supplied envelopes.

| Alternative | Calculated interfaces and consequence |
|---|---|
| Two unfiltered direct RF sample channels, 2.5 GS/s, 14 bits, 1.2 W/channel +0.4 W common | 70 Gbit/s raw and 2.8 W; fails link/power, no-selector gain interval and single-baseline ambiguity |
| Two analog-converted long-baseline channels, 100 MS/s, 0.6 W/channel +0.2 W selectors +0.4 W common | 1.8 W; at 10% transport overhead, 3.08 Gbit/s; gain passes but direction remains ambiguous |
| Three simultaneous short/long analog-converted channels, same per-channel envelope | 2.4 W; 4.2 Gbit/s raw and 4.62 Gbit/s at 10% overhead; passes supplied resource, gain and idealized information constraints |
| One analog beam output without another observable | Potential resource saving remains unspecified; one unknown complex source amplitude makes a single combined response insufficient for direction |

The 0.2 W selector allowance is total for the selected branch, not per channel.
The 0.4 W common allowance includes reference/control within this envelope.
For three channels, allowable framing overhead is at most
$5/4.2-1=19.0476$ percent; 25 percent would exceed the link even though the
analog and information calculations still pass. A driver that does not see
50 Ω invalidates the power-to-voltage conversion; the prescribed 0.100 V peak
limit must be translated to its actual differential/common-mode/load interface.
No part has been selected on these numbers.

Direct sampling can also use RF preselection. The rejected row is the specified
unfiltered implementation, not a limitation inherent in direct sampling. Adding
selection would address its headroom conflict, but would not by itself reduce
70 Gbit/s raw traffic, its supplied power or a single long baseline's ambiguity.

@fig-architecture-interfaces places the constraints at their physical interfaces.
Calibration injection after a selector does not measure its response or the
field manifold. Retaining all three complex channels allows relative-response
checks and later reprocessing; combining before observing them trades that access

these endpoints: independent sources add relative offset/drift unless estimated,
whereas a shared source still has distribution delay and reset-sensitive branch
phase. The present 0.4 W reference allowance establishes neither alternative's
physical performance.

An endpoint comparison makes the remaining reference conditions calculable.

the later correlated allocation must reconcile them with calibration and the

channel, with the 20 MHz IF already specified.

# Verification and Acceptance Standard

**Status:** provisional.

## What evidence establishes
- Algebraic/symbolic checks support mathematical consistency under encoded assumptions.
- Unit tests support implementation correctness for tested cases.
- Limiting cases, independent derivations, reference comparisons and convergence checks broaden confidence but do not automatically validate physics.
- Physical validation requires representative empirical evidence with stated domain and uncertainty.
- Requirements compliance is specific to the implemented system and its specified conditions.

## Risk-proportionate review
Use stronger independent methods for consequential system budgets, synchronization promises, phase-noise models, calibration identifiability and acceptance criteria. Do not treat repeated AI reasoning as independent physical evidence.

## Technical states
- **Draft:** unaccepted material.
- **Checked:** specific mechanical/mathematical/computational checks recorded.
- **Reviewed:** an engineer examined relevant reasoning and limitations.
- **Accepted for stated use:** human decision backed by adequate evidence; may later be restricted or superseded.
These labels are not identical to evidence type or publication readiness.

## Minimum acceptance information
Claim and intended use, assumptions, evidence/checks executed, important uncertainties, blocking issues, reviewing engineer and date/revision if formally accepted. Never fabricate a review record or claim human acceptance.

## Pilot checks and educational assessment

For consequential calculations compare distinct formulations, appropriate limits,
units, convergence and sampling error. A seeded simulation is reproducible, not
independent physical evidence. Code and analytical formulas sharing an assumption
cannot validate that assumption. Record unavailable dependencies and failed
commands as well as successful checks.

A reader assessment requires an actual RF-engineer participant to define a
measurand, calculate a decision, reject a misleading result, change the model for
a new topology/observation, and find applicability conditions. Record assistance,
reasoning errors and revisions; a small trial cannot establish general learning
effectiveness. A critical reference/sign/correlation/observability error requires
revision and reassessment. Authorial self-check is not specialist review.

Final human acceptance states separately: planning suitability; mathematical
correctness under assumptions; physical applicability; educational/practical
adequacy; experimental confirmation; and compliance for a named implementation.
Missing review or empirical evidence remains pending rather than inferred.

## Review of connections and task closure

Challenge the connections between observable, physical model, calculation,
implementation/procedure and evidence, not just the individual formulas. Use
asymmetric inputs or changed references/operators where symmetry can hide a defect.
Record correction propagation to dependent results and repeat affected checks.
A bounded task may close as a completed, checked provisional draft with human
review pending; this is distinct from human technical acceptance and publication
integration. Assess physical applicability separately; theoretical identities do
not universally require laboratory tests, while hardware-performance claims need
representative evidence. Publication integration additionally needs reading-path,
notation, cross-reference and rendered-presentation review for the intended edition.

## Separate-context AI review

AI review is additional evidence, not the human **Reviewed** state. Use a fresh
conversation with no author history or correctness assertions. Freeze input bytes
and record SHA-256 when HEAD does not identify them. Give the reviewer accepted
requirements, manuscript, applicable standards and actual source access; inspect
reasoning before author check code. Seek alternative derivations, limiting cases,
asymmetric counterexamples and failures of assumptions, reference planes and
engineering interpretation.

Classify findings as demonstrated errors, model/applicability concerns, missing
evidence, pedagogical defects or optional improvements. Record location, consequence,
evidence, author disposition, correction propagation and reassessment. Identify AI
model/effort/session, sources actually examined, checks run and unperformed checks.
A separate context using the same model retains correlated failure risks. Review
failure blocks progression; unavailable evidence restricts dependent claims.

## Visual-adequacy gate for bounded teaching units

Assess scientific correctness and pedagogical communication separately. Check
quantitative curves through independent formulations, limits and spot values;
check schematic paths, signs, planes and correlation against the model. Follow
[the actual-image procedure](../docs/VISUAL-INSPECTION.md): inspect standalone pixels
and the complete rendered page with readable detail crops, equations and captions.
Fresh read-only AI review receives actual raster attachments and frozen models;
record image access, readability limits, findings and correction reassessment.
Source parsing, successful capture and render success alone never clear this gate.

A missing indispensable explanation, consequential model/graphical error, unreadable
figure, failed image inspection or unresolved consequential review finding blocks
a positive visual-adequacy recommendation. Optional polish can remain documented.
AI visual review does not grant human acceptance, reader-trial evidence or physical
validation, and does not authorize subsequent canonical authoring.

# Notation and Conventions

**Status:** initial proposal; canonical conventions must be reviewed before substantive mathematical chapters.

## Proposed conventions to confirm
- Continuous-time Fourier transform: `X(f) = ∫ x(t) exp(-j 2π f t) dt` and inverse with `+j 2π f t`.
- Angular frequency `ω = 2π f`, frequency `f` in hertz.
- Real physical waveforms vs complex analytical signals/envelopes must carry explicit scaling and carrier-sign conventions.
- Unwrapped phase and circular/angle-valued statistics are distinct; specify the one used.
- Spectral densities: explicitly state one-/two-sided definition, variable, units, domain and cross-spectrum ordering.
- Time and phase reference planes, trigger/reset state, bandwidth/filter and observation interval must accompany consequential phase measures.
- Clearly distinguish power and amplitude ratios in dB, and RMS vs peak conventions.

## Unresolved choices
General complex-envelope normalization, default PSD convention, phase-noise `L(f)` normalization, cross-spectrum sign/order, treatment of distributional/nonstationary spectra. Do **not** silently resolve these by defaulting to whatever an external source uses.

## Relative-phase pilot conventions (local selection; review pending)

These explicit local choices permit a reviewable draft; they are not accepted
book-wide defaults. Human mathematical/engineering review remains outstanding.

- `v(t)=Re{z(t) exp(j 2π fc t)}`; z has peak-voltage scaling. For a constant
  envelope into a declared resistance R, power is `|z|²/(2R)`.
- Relative phase is channel 2 relative to 1: `arg(z2 conj(z1))`.
- Use the proposed Fourier pair above. Define centered correlation
  `Rxy(τ)=E[(x(t+τ)-μx) conj(y(t)-μy)]` and its transform `Sxy`.
  Thus `Sxy` corresponds to `X conj(Y)` and `Syx=conj(Sxy)`.
- Derivations use two-sided spectra over all real offset frequencies, in
  rad²/Hz for phase. State band limits explicitly. Imported one-sided spectra
  require an explicit conversion; no universal L(f) conversion is selected.
- A physical delay has transfer `exp(-j 2π f τ)`; group delay is the negative
  phase derivative with respect to angular frequency. State RF versus offset f.
- Unwrapped residuals require continuity and amplitude/SNR conditions; otherwise
  use circular quantities and report slips, gaps and invalid intervals.
- Noise spectra describe centered processes. Deterministic drift, spurs and
  restart-state mixtures are kept separate. Positive time error here means an
  advance, `φ/(2π fc)`; a physical delay has the opposite phase sign.

General normalization, nonstationary/distributional spectral theory and unrelated
convention choices remain unresolved. Translate each source rather than silently

**Status:** provisional.

Each substantial treatment should motivate an engineering question, develop relevant physics and mathematics, define assumptions, interpret results, demonstrate their engineering use, and disclose limitations. Different subjects need different structures: do not impose a mechanical template on all chapters.

- Develop prerequisites or add a targeted mathematical refresher where general RF expertise is insufficient.
- Use complete derivations for essential results; distinguish exact statements from approximations.
- Include system interactions, contrasting architectures and counterexamples where important.
- Use readable diagrams that correctly indicate signal paths, reference planes, directions and units.
- Integrate physical implementation, calibration and verification implications close to the relevant theory.
- Prefer a canonical result with sensible local exposition/cross-reference over copying conflicting derivations.
- Never invent numerical component data or use arbitrary design parameters without labeling them illustrative.

     2	
     3	A receiver can have enough gain, a precise phase estimate and a fast data link,
     4	yet still fail its task. The gain may clip the blocker, the phase may select the
     5	wrong spatial branch, or the estimate may arrive after the scene has changed.
     6	Architecture selection starts by intersecting these conditions at the same
     7	operating point. A favorable calculation in each of several incompatible states
     8	is not a feasible receiver.

    10	This bounded development asks whether a small direction-comparison receiver can
    11	meet a supplied angular, blocker and response-time brief. The reader should be
    12	able to turn a need into a conditioned observable, calculate incompatible gain

    14	which missing evidence prevents a hardware recommendation. Requirement framing
    15	begins in [Chapter 1](phase-comparison.qmd#sec-requirement-framing). We use

    86	### Gain does not create headroom
    87	
    88	First intersect weak-tone visibility and composite-input survival. Let $G$ be
    89	the conversion/voltage-chain **power gain in dB** between equal 50 Ω reference
    90	planes, $L_s$ the wanted insertion loss, and $A_B$ the blocker's total RF
    91	attenuation in dB. At the gain input, powers in milliwatts are
    92	
    93	$$
    94	 p_s=10^{(-100-L_s)/10},\qquad p_b=10^{(-20-A_B)/10}.
    95	$$
    96	
    97	With worst relative tone phase, the peak voltage is proportional to
    98	$\sqrt{p_s}+\sqrt{p_b}$. Thus the equivalent composite peak power before gain is
    99	$p_{\rm pk}=(\sqrt{p_s}+\sqrt{p_b})^2$, and the two bounds are
   100	
   101	$$
   102	 G_{\min}=-60-(-100-L_s)=40+L_s,\qquad
   103	 G_{\max}=-10-10\log_{10}p_{\rm pk}.
   104	$$
   105	
   106	This is a peak constraint, not an incoherent addition of average powers. For
   107	more carriers replace the two amplitudes by a justified envelope or crest-factor
   108	bound. Gain must exist in $[G_{\min},G_{\max}]$ and every intermediate stage must
   109	also survive the waveform. Final-output headroom alone cannot establish that.
   110	
   111	With no preselection, $L_s=A_B=0$: the bounds are 40 and 9.99913 dB. Their
   112	intersection is empty by approximately 30 dB. A digital blocker notch after
   113	sampling cannot restore clipped information. Now supply a selector family with
   114	$L_s=2$ dB, and choose $A_B=40$ dB. The bounds become 42 and 49.93128 dB.
   115	At $G=46$ dB, wanted and blocker powers at P2 are −56 and −14 dBm; the
   116	worst composite is −13.93128 dBm, within the supplied −10 dBm limit.
   117	The gain interval is now nonempty, conditional on linearity and noise evidence.

   129	### Information, ambiguity and available time
   130	
   131	A baseline $d$ along the array axis has relative field phase
   132	$\phi=kd\sin\theta$, where $k=2\pi/\lambda$, using Chapter 8's sourceward
   133	geometry and Chapter 1's normalized orientation. A phase report is modulo $2\pi$.
   134	To avoid two noiseless directions in the closed sector sharing the same phase,
   135	require
   136	
   137	$$
   138	 2kd\sin60^\circ<2\pi,\qquad
   139	 d<d_{\rm amb}={\lambda\over2\sin60^\circ}=0.173205\ \mathrm m.
   140	$$
   141	
   142	The inequality is strict: equality aliases the two sector endpoints. This is a
   143	single-baseline, single-frequency result under the supplied manifold, not a
   144	universal aperture limit.
   145	
   146	For a sufficiently strong tone with proper Gaussian complex noise, Chapter 2's
   147	small-noise phase approximation gives per-channel phase variance $1/(2\rho)$.
   148	Independent equal-noise channels therefore have relative-phase variance
   149	$1/\rho$. Linearizing the phase-angle relation gives
   150	
   151	$$
   152	 \sigma_\theta\simeq{1\over kd|\cos\theta|\sqrt\rho},\qquad
   153	 d\geq d_{\rm prec}={1\over k|\cos\theta|\sigma_{\theta,\max}\sqrt\rho}.
   154	$$
   155	
   156	Use radians in this calculation. At the edge approached from inside the sector,
   157	$|\cos\theta|=1/2$, $\sigma_{\theta,\max}=0.00872665$ rad and $\rho=100$:
   158	$d_{\rm prec}=1.094269$ m. There is no baseline satisfying both 1.094269 m
   159	minimum precision aperture and 0.173205 m maximum unambiguous baseline. A local
   160	precision calculation alone would have selected a globally ambiguous design.
   161	The linearized uncertainty is conditional on the correct branch; it is not a
   162	Gaussian model for arbitrarily large angle errors or an edge-clipped estimator.
   163	
   164	Increasing gain does not improve this input-referred SNR when signal and dominant
   165	analog noise are amplified together. Increasing observation time can improve
   166	energy, but the time must exist. For a normalized rectangular tone observation
   167	with residual frequency $\delta f$, direct integration of
   168	$T^{-1}\int_0^T e^{j2\pi\delta f t}dt$ gives amplitude
   169	$e^{j\pi\delta fT}\operatorname{sinc}(\delta fT)$, with
   170	$\operatorname{sinc}x=\sin(\pi x)/(\pi x)$. Consequently
   171	
   172	$$
   173	 \rho(T,\delta f)=(10^5\,\mathrm{Hz})T\operatorname{sinc}^2(\delta fT).
   174	$$
   175	
   176	This is an explicit observation model, not a universal integration-loss rule.
   177	The constant-manifold excursion requirement gives $T\leq0.05/20=2.5$ ms;
   178	latency alone gives $T\leq4.4$ ms. Thus 2.5 ms is the tighter supplied limit.
   179	A short baseline $d_s=0.150$ m would need $\rho=5321.885$ even before other
   180	errors: 53.21885 ms at zero offset. It cannot obtain that energy within the
   181	brief. At 100 Hz residual offset and 1 ms, $\rho=96.75312$ rather than 100.
   182	Both the wanted response and noise normalization must follow the observation.
   183	
   184	@fig-aperture-feasibility makes the precision/ambiguity conflict visible.
   185	A 1.2 m baseline meets the local 0.5° target at 1 ms, but its wrapped phase
   186	cannot select the correct direction. A 0.15 m baseline resolves the sector but
   187	cannot meet that precision with the available energy. More information, a
   188	restricted sector, a changed deadline/energy envelope or another measured
   189	observable is needed.

   193	## Architecture and quantitative interfaces {#sec-architecture-interfaces}
   194	
   195	Consider three simultaneous ports at positions 0, 0.15 and 1.20 m. The long
   196	baseline supplies local precision, while the short baseline supplies a coarse
   197	sector estimate. This is a bounded ambiguity-restoration example, not a complete
   198	bearing estimator or a claim that three elements solve multipath/polarization.
   199	The source amplitude/common phase is a nuisance removed by relative comparisons.
   200	A single analog-combined complex output cannot generally recover direction from
   201	one unknown complex source amplitude: for any nonzero combined response $b(u)$,
   202	its change can be absorbed into that amplitude. Multiple independent beam outputs
   203	or scans can restore information, but their timing and manifold must be budgeted.
   204	Analog reception is a valid alternative when those interfaces are supplied.
   205	
   206	For the selected simultaneous case let $u=\sin\theta$ and
   207	$\Delta u=\lambda/d_l=0.25$ be long-baseline branch spacing. Fine candidates
   208	come from adding integer cycles to its phase; select the one nearest the short
   209	baseline's direction cosine. Ignoring channel-noise correlation would misstate
   210	that decision's uncertainty: both differences contain the reference channel.
   211	If individual small phase errors $\epsilon_0,\epsilon_s,\epsilon_l$ are
   212	independent with variance $1/(2\rho)$, the branch-comparison error is
   213	
   214	$$
   215	 e_u={\epsilon_s-\epsilon_0\over kd_s}
   216	       -{\epsilon_l-\epsilon_0\over kd_l},\qquad
   217	 \sigma_{e_u}^2={1\over\rho}
   218	 \left[{1\over(kd_s)^2}+{1\over(kd_l)^2}-{1\over(kd_s)(kd_l)}\right].
   219	$$
   220	
   221	The cross term follows from the shared $\epsilon_0$ source; it is not an arbitrary
   222	correlation coefficient. In the high-SNR Gaussian phase approximation,
   223	$2\Phi[-\Delta u/(2\sigma_{e_u})]$ bounds a nearest-branch error when the coarse
   224	phase has not wrapped, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF. To avoid treating
   225	that qualification as automatic, add a coarse-wrap bound. The minimum distance
   226	to its principal-phase boundary over the sector is
   227	$m=\pi-kd_s\sin60^\circ$. A conservative union bound is
   228	
   229	$$
   230	 P_{\rm branch}\ \lesssim\
   231	 2\Phi\!\left(-{\Delta u\over2\sigma_{e_u}}\right)
   232	 +2\Phi(-m\sqrt\rho).
   233	$$
   234	
   235	The approximate sign recalls the linear Gaussian phase model, not a measured
   236	error rate. At 1 ms and worst 100 Hz residual offset, the two terms are
   237	$4.258\times10^{-5}$ and $3.472\times10^{-5}$, totaling less than
   238	$7.74\times10^{-5}$, below the supplied $10^{-3}$ limit. The long-baseline
   239	local uncertainty is approximately 0.46353°. No calibration, multipath or state
   240	error has yet been charged; the apparent margin is not available twice.
   241	A branch failure is a large error event, not another small term to RSS into 0.46353°.

   252	Receiver passband width is not a statement of stopband rejection.

## From a comparison to a receiver requirement {#sec-requirement-framing}

Before specifying “coherent channels,” state the operation the comparison must
support. A burst receiver may need a usable payload decision before its deadline;
a phase instrument may need a corrected port ratio over a stated record. Those
are different outcomes even when both contain an internal phase comparison.
A requirement should identify the observable and its units, physical/reference
planes, filtering and interval, signal/blocker envelope, operating state and
calibration history, a limit, and the evidence that could test it. An unspecified
limit remains a question, not permission to choose a convenient value.

For example, “relative phase within 2°” is incomplete. Is it an instantaneous
error, a centered RMS fluctuation over a band, an uncertainty in an averaged
ratio, or a restart-to-restart intercept? Are invalid-amplitude intervals excluded,
and must the signal remain usable after a retune? A common clock addresses none
of these distinctions by itself. A coherent solution should be compared with a
noncoherent one using the actual task outcome, not coherence as a preference.

For a concrete choice, suppose a burst only needs an on/off energy decision and
its carrier phase is unknown. An energy observation such as an integrated
squared voltage can support that task while discarding phase; its noise law,
threshold, timing and false-alarm performance still need specification. A
phase-sensitive port instrument instead needs the complex channel ratio:
separate channel energies do not retain its relative phase, even if their energy
decisions are excellent. A known phase change at one input can distinguish these
claims experimentally: the ratio should follow it while the ideal energy remains
unchanged. Conversely vary level/noise and test the burst decision probabilities.
These are proposed evidence routes, not performed experiments; later detection
theory supplies the conditional calculations.

Consider a phase-sensitive port measurement after a restart. Connector injection
can test part of the electronic transfer under that state; it cannot establish
an external propagation path. Record what is held fixed and what changed before
claiming repeatability. For an array, a highly precise wrapped phase can still
identify several directions. The [feasibility treatment](feasibility-architecture-allocations.qmd)
turns these distinctions into intersecting quantitative constraints once the
necessary physical and statistical models are available. At this first framing,
missing waveform, ambiguity, dynamic, headroom and evidence conditions should
be exposed rather than silently filled in.

def gain_bounds(blocker_attenuation=40,wanted_loss=2):
    """dB bounds at equal50ohm planes; two-tone worst composite voltage."""
    ps=10**((-100-wanted_loss)/10)
    pb=10**((-20-blocker_attenuation)/10)
    return 40+wanted_loss,-10-20*log10(sqrt(ps)+sqrt(pb))


def aperture_limits(rho=100):
    k=2*pi/.3
    return 1/(k*.5*radians(.5)*sqrt(rho)),.3/(2*sin(pi/3))


def requirement_case():
    k=2*pi/.3;ds=.15;dl=1.2;rho=100*sinc(.1)**2
    variance=(1/(k*ds)**2+1/(k*dl)**2-1/(k*ds*k*dl))/rho
    nd=NormalDist();m=pi-k*ds*sin(pi/3)
    terms=(2*nd.cdf(-.3/(2*dl)/sqrt(variance)),2*nd.cdf(-m*sqrt(rho)))
    return {'rho':rho,'gain_bounds':gain_bounds(),
            'fine_sigma_degrees':degrees(1/(k*dl*.5*sqrt(rho))),
            'branch_terms':terms,'branch_sum':sum(terms),
            'short_rho':1/(k*ds*.5*radians(.5))**2}


def retained_blocker(eta=1e-5):
    """Composite path-magnitude contract; high-SNR phase approximation."""
    from math import asin
    k=2*pi/.3;rho=requirement_case()['rho'];r=10**(42/20)*eta
    beta=asin(r);minimum_rho=rho*(1-r)**2
    a,b=1/(k*.15),1/(k*1.2)
    sd=sqrt((a*a+b*b-a*b)/minimum_rho)
    bu=2*beta*(a+b);m=pi-k*.15*sin(pi/3)
    nd=NormalDist()
    return {'r':r,'beta':beta,'minimum_rho':minimum_rho,
            'local_sigma_degrees':degrees(1/(k*1.2*.5*sqrt(minimum_rho))),
            'local_bias_degrees':degrees(2*beta/(k*1.2*.5)),
            'branch_bound':2*nd.cdf(-(.125-bu)/sd)+2*nd.cdf(-(m-2*beta)*sqrt(minimum_rho))}

item.text:
The targeted reassessment found **no consequential mathematical or visual defect in the new calculations under their stated assumptions**. The candidate remains conditionally feasible. Unknown rejection, reference, calibration, loading, noise and implementation interfaces prevent an evidenced receiver-performance claim.

I read the requirements, applicable standards, source excerpts/notes and manuscript before examining the relevant model and test code. Independent calculations preceded code comparison. All **162 SHA-256 manifest entries matched**, including a final verification. This establishes consistency with the supplied manifest; it does not authenticate provenance or prove that every raster exactly reproduces the accompanying HTML.

The [composite rejection contract](/tmp/k1113/k11c-input/book/feasibility-architecture-allocations.qmd:254) correctly covers the complete blocker-to-record response: frequency uncertainty, conversion/filtering, real-signal images, alias routes and finite observation. Bounding the **sum of path magnitudes** supports a worst-phase triangle bound without assuming independent paths or favorable cancellation. Multiplying the post-selector amplitude ratio \(125.8925\) by \(10^{-5}\) gives \(r=0.0012589254\). The intended reference is the post-selector blocker/wanted ratio; implementation evidence must preserve that normalization and the wanted response.

A separate sampled-real-tone calculation confirms why this contract needs independent evidence. With 100 MS/s, a 1 ms record, a 20 MHz observation reference, wanted frequency 20 MHz + 100 Hz and blocker frequency 10 MHz + 100 Hz, the two blocker image contributions have a normalized magnitude sum about \(1.405\times10^{-5}\) before additional filtering. Thus nominal frequency placement or an exact nominal rectangular-window null does not automatically establish \(10^{-5}\) rejection across the allowed offsets. This does not contradict the manuscript: it explicitly supplies rejection as an interface and leaves its realization unknown. The changed-condition 100.5 kHz example independently gives retained amplitude \(0.3987347\), consistent with the text.

The [phasor-disk construction](/tmp/k1113/k11c-input/book/feasibility-architecture-allocations.qmd:266) is sound. Cartesian tangency gives the contact point
\[
(1-r^2,\;r\sqrt{1-r^2}),
\]
whose angle is \(\arcsin r\); the nearest disk point has magnitude \(1-r\). Numerical phase sweeps independently reproduce both extrema. Allowing each channel its own bounded contamination gives relative-phase bias at most \(2\arcsin r\). Exact inverse-manifold evaluation at 60° gives outward angular displacement about **0.011482°**, supporting the stated “about 0.01149°” and remaining below 0.02°. The blocker plot’s allocation threshold also agrees with exact geometry: \(r\approx0.00219258\), corresponding to approximately 95.181 dB rejection.

The recomputed noise and branch treatment remains conservative **within the linear Gaussian phase approximation**. Expanding the three independent channel errors gives coefficients \(a\), \(-c\) and \(c-a\), where \(a=1/(kd_s)\) and \(c=1/(kd_l)\). Their squared coefficients recover the manuscript’s negative covariance cross term. Even when contamination produces unequal channel amplitudes, each phase-noise variance is bounded by using the minimum amplitude \(1-r\); this justifies the common reduced-SNR envelope. I obtain:

- \(\rho=96.7531209\), and \(\rho_{\min}=96.5096643\).
- Local standard uncertainty \(0.4641169^\circ\).
- Biased nearest-branch term \(4.94120\times10^{-5}\).
- Coarse-wrap term \(3.95496\times10^{-5}\).
- Union total **\(8.89616\times10^{-5}\)**.

The bias allowances subtract from positive decision margins, and the union bound requires no independence between its events. The text appropriately avoids presenting this approximate tail calculation as a measured or rigorous nonlinear rare-event guarantee.

The [reference comparison](/tmp/k1113/k11c-input/book/feasibility-architecture-allocations.qmd:338) reproduces correctly: 0.05° over 1 ms permits 0.136166 ps LO differential-delay change at 1.020 GHz, 0.138889 Hz relative LO offset, 6.94444 ps sample-epoch change, or fractional rate error \(6.94444\times10^{-9}\). One 10 ns sample displacement corresponds to 72° at 20 MHz. These are excursion magnitudes; signed corrections must follow the declared conversion orientation and channel ordering. The 0 dBm/50 Ω drive example gives 0.316228 V peak, and three separately loss-compensated 6 dB branches require 11.9432 mW at the stated source-side planes. The manuscript properly separates these RF powers from unspecified driver consumption and leaves independent-reference acquisition, residuals and latency unresolved.

The engineering framing is appropriately bounded. The rejected direct-sampling alternative is explicitly the supplied **unfiltered implementation**; preselection remains available to direct sampling. Traffic, power and ambiguity remain separate constraints. The 2.4 W and 4.62 Gbit/s selected-envelope calculations reproduce. Post-selector injection correctly excludes field and selector response. Chapter 1’s [new framing](/tmp/k1113/k11c-input/book/phase-comparison.qmd:311) makes a concrete distinction between energy decisions and complex-ratio measurements, with suitable phase-perturbation, level/noise and restart evidence routes. Its ideal energy-invariance statement should be understood with the specified observation/filtering convention.

I inspected **all 22 actual PNGs**: `figure1–4`, both full pages, `k11c0-crop00–08` and `k11c1-crop00–06`. Full pages supported layout inspection; readable crops supported equation and table inspection. Curves, baseline scale, tangent geometry, interface arrows, captions and conditional claims agree with the model.
